name: Wild chamomile
grown_as: William's library gives Matricaria discoidea, which is pineappleweed: a wild annual with no white rays, common on paths and trodden ground, and it is in his kitchen garden. Described here as that. ⚠️ CHECK: the name 'wild chamomile' is more often used for Matricaria chamomilla (scented mayweed or German chamomile), which has white rays round a hollow yellow cone. If that is what was sown, this file and the drawings need redoing.
habit: A low, bushy, much-branched annual 5 to 30 cm, often flattened where trodden. Smells strongly of pineapple when crushed.

leaf.type: Simple but divided two or three times (pinnately) into very narrow, thread-like segments

flower.form: A small, rounded to egg-shaped cone of tiny florets with no white rays at all
flower.petals: None that show: all the florets are tiny tubes with four teeth
flower.centre: The whole head is a solid dome of florets on a hollow cone-shaped base
flower.behind: Short green bracts with broad pale papery edges, much shorter than the head
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of short branches, many to a plant, facing up

fruit: The heads turn brown and crumble. Seeds tiny, about 1.5 mm, pale brown and ribbed, with a narrow papery rim at the top; they stick to wet shoes and tyres.
seedling: Two tiny oval seed leaves. The first true leaves are already finely divided and feathery.
winter: Nothing, or small seedlings over winter in mild spells.

leaf: leaf divided two or three times into thread-like segments, feathery
bloom: a rounded cone of tiny greenish-yellow florets
short bracts with broad pale papery edges round the base
young: small low tuft of bright green feathery leaves
flower: many small greenish-yellow cone heads on short stalks
seedhead: heads turned brown, cone-shaped and crumbling

look_alikes: Scented mayweed (Matricaria chamomilla) has white rays that turn down round a hollow cone. Scentless mayweed has white rays and a solid disc. Tansy has button heads without rays but is a tall perennial with broad toothed leaflets. Corn chamomile has white rays and grey downy leaves.
